name: Pale Brownish Drab
lede: Pale Brownish Drab is a grayish, yellowish pink from Ridgway's 1912 plates, measured in our color graph as identical to a separately sourced Dark Silver Pink, and common across our painting archive.

sections.title: One grey-pink, several near-duplicates
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* places this hue at plate XLV, hue 9′′′′, tone d, scanned from an aged plate and so approximate [1]. The ISCC-NBS system later filed it in its own block [1]. Our color graph finds a separately recorded name, Dark Silver Pink, at zero units of difference, an exact duplicate under a different name, and our library separately notes two further near-duplicates on adjacent Ridgway chips, Pale Vinaceous-Drab and Ecru-Drab [2].

The nearest named colors on file are [[pale-purple-drab]], [[sweet-pea]], [[pale-ecru-drab]] and [[greyish-tan]], at 3.5, 3.8, 3.9 and 4.5 ΔE [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, a color within six units of Pale Brownish Drab covers at least five per cent of a canvas in 640 works, more common than 81 per cent of our named colors [4]. The painter most devoted to it is Xugu, in 6 of his 16 works here, about 6.4 times his museums' baseline [4]. It most often shares a canvas with [[rocket-metallic]] and Mole brown, at 16.7 and 6.3 times the expected rate [4]. The earliest dated appearance in our archive is the year 1000, nine centuries before the name's own 1912 record, a look-alike hue, not proof of pigment, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4]. These remain photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors [4].
